name: Architecture decisions should be documented
rationale: Important architecture decisions are easier to revisit when recorded with context, options, and consequences.
remediation: Add docs/architecture and ADRs for significant decisions.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Core/domain logic should not depend on infrastructure details
rationale: Stable business rules should be insulated from volatile details such as databases, APIs, frameworks, and UI.
remediation: Introduce ports/interfaces in core/application layer and move concrete implementations to infrastructure/adapters.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Feature or domain modules should have clear ownership
rationale: Modular boundaries reduce change blast radius and prepare a monolith for future extraction only if needed.
remediation: Group code by feature/domain and document module contracts.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Architecture-sensitive areas need tests before refactoring
rationale: Untested code should be characterized before structural changes to avoid edit-and-pray refactoring.
remediation: Add characterization tests around behavior before changing architecture.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Configuration and secrets should be externalized
rationale: Hard-coded secrets/config make deployments unsafe and environments hard to manage.
remediation: Move secrets/config to environment variables, secret stores, or config files excluded from version control.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Operational code should include logging and explicit error handling
rationale: Systems are easier to operate and debug when failures are visible and intentional.
remediation: Add structured logging and explicit handling for network, filesystem, database, and provider failures.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Data ownership and migrations should be explicit
rationale: Data architecture is often the hardest part to change after product growth.
remediation: Document data ownership, schema changes, migrations, retention, and consistency expectations.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: WordPress hooks should be thin and delegate to services
rationale: Hook-heavy procedural files become difficult to test and maintain; hooks should adapt WordPress events into application services.
remediation: Keep root plugin file small. Move behavior into classes/services and protect admin actions with nonce/capability checks.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Android UI state and business logic should be separated
rationale: Android apps need lifecycle-aware boundaries to stay testable and maintainable as screens grow.
remediation: Use ViewModel/repository/use-case boundaries. Consider multi-module structure for growing apps.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: AI providers, prompts, and models should be configurable and reproducible
rationale: AI systems are hard to debug if prompts/model parameters are scattered and not versioned.
remediation: Centralize prompt templates, model configuration, provider adapters, cache keys, and evaluation fixtures.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: New code should pass automated quality gates
rationale: Clean-as-you-change governance prevents new debt while legacy code is improved gradually.
remediation: Add CI for tests, linting, architecture scan, and security checks appropriate for the stack.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Swift UI layer should not own business workflows
evidence: SwiftUI View or UIKit controller references URLSession, file IO, persistence, analytics, AI provider, or payment SDK directly
rationale: Swift UI code should remain composable and testable; IO and business workflows belong behind state, use-case, service, or reducer boundaries.
recommendation: Move workflow logic into ViewModel/store/use case/service; inject protocols/adapters; add tests around state transitions and service behavior.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Swift features should have explicit package/module boundaries when growing
evidence: Many Swift files with no feature folders, no Packages directory, and no module ownership docs
rationale: Feature/package boundaries reduce change blast radius and make AI-generated edits safer.
recommendation: Introduce feature folders or Swift packages for domain/app core/features/infrastructure; document module contracts.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Rust binary entrypoints should be thin
evidence: Large src/main.rs or main.rs with core workflow, IO orchestration, parsing, and business logic mixed together
rationale: Library-first Rust projects are easier to test, reuse, benchmark, and evolve.
recommendation: Move core workflows to src/lib.rs/modules or workspace crates; keep main.rs focused on CLI/config/top-level error reporting.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Unsafe Rust must be treated as an architectural boundary
evidence: unsafe blocks/functions/traits without nearby safety comments, invariants, or tests
rationale: Unsafe code can bypass Rust safety guarantees, so its assumptions must be explicit and reviewable.
recommendation: Add SAFETY comments, isolate unsafe code, test invariants, and consider Miri/fuzzing where appropriate.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Rust dependency risk should be audited
evidence: Cargo.lock exists without cargo-deny/cargo-audit or equivalent dependency policy
rationale: Rust projects can rely on many transitive dependencies; advisories, licenses, duplicate crates, and source policies should be visible.
recommendation: Add cargo-deny or equivalent dependency audit to CI; document allowed licenses and banned crates/sources.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Framework self-improvement must preserve core rule integrity
evidence: New examples or findings proposed as core rule changes without validation, references, or counterexamples
rationale: A review framework becomes noisy if every example mutates the core model. Learning must happen through evidence, profiles, adapters, and validation before core promotion.
recommendation: Add proposed changes as experimental rules or product-profile mappings first; require references, example repos, false-positive review, and changelog entry before promotion.
reference_scope: methodological inspiration; source does not endorse rule or numeric threshold

name: Browser extension permissions should be proportionate
rationale: Broad extension host permissions increase the potential impact of a defect or compromise.
remediation: Prefer narrowly scoped or optional host permissions and document necessary exceptions.
reference_scope: Architecture guidance; does not validate heuristic accuracy

name: Google Apps Script entrypoints should delegate IO
rationale: Thin triggers ease quota management and testing of external integrations.
remediation: Delegate integration logic from triggers to testable services.
reference_scope: Architecture guidance; does not validate heuristic accuracy

name: npm libraries need explicit public entrypoint
rationale: Package consumers need clear public exports or executable entrypoints.
remediation: Define exports/main/bin as appropriate and validate packed artifact.
reference_scope: Architecture guidance; does not validate heuristic accuracy
